name: SENSEI Skipper-CCD detector
notes: The device changed generations over the experiment's history (0.0947 g protoSENSEI in 2019 to a ~2 g Skipper-CCD from 2020); no single 'current' mass/pixel count as of 2026 was found in the sources fetched.

placements.note: Placed at the existing site:fermilab-main-campus (owned by fermilab-dune), which that lead's own notes already use as the campus-precision placement for the Fermilab MINOS near-detector hall (kind: detector, precision_m 3000); no source fetched this session gives a more precise coordinate for this specific cavern.
placements.quote: a prototype Skipper-CCD placed in the MINOS cavern, ... at the Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory (FNAL)

active_mass.note: This is the protoSENSEI (2019) device's mass; the 2020 device was ~2 g (see notes). No mass figure for the current (2026) detector was found in the papers fetched this session.
active_mass.quote: a total active mass (before masking) of 0.0947 gram

pixel_count.note: Computed from the quoted quadrant geometry (4 quadrants x 624 rows x 362 pixels), not stated as a single total in the source.
pixel_count.quote: each consisting of 624 rows of 362 pixels

summary.plain: A tiny silicon chip called a skipper CCD, sensitive enough to count single electrons, sitting in a shielded underground hall at Fermilab to catch the faint signal of a very light dark matter particle.
summary.technical: Skipper-CCD detector operated in the MINOS cavern at Fermilab; protoSENSEI (2018-2019) had 0.0947 g active mass across ~898,000 pixels in four amplifier quadrants, superseded by a ~2 g high-resistivity Skipper-CCD from 2020, with operations continuing as of 2026.

technology.quote: Skipper Charge-Coupled Devices (Skipper-CCDs) are a leading technology in the search for sub-GeV dark matter
technology.value: Skipper charge-coupled device (CCD): a high-resistivity silicon CCD with sub-electron readout noise, counting individual ionization electrons
